plan_review.notes: Alt A second scheduler rejected: would duplicate route/budget authority. Alt B whole-BT utility selector rejected: tactical safety ordering remains valid. Alt C scenario-only scorer rejected: shared deterministic portfolio contract is needed, but v1 remains bounded to existing Floor 1 graph producers plus Floor 2 settlement candidate. Alt D extend current planner adopted: add utility/portfolio semantics to the exact planner rather than a competing DSL. Resolutions: explicit AI strategic affinity config; preserve optional bundle verdicts; settlement router retains latch/cooldown/fingerprint ownership and emits a candidate; cover every decision-mode consumer; separate portfolio-choice invalidation from route feasibility; explicit v1 floor scope; explicit committed-active-objective state with completion/invalidity release.

rounds.notes: 1) A partially populated ObjectiveUtilityWeights object silently produced NaN utility scores, collapsing portfolio selection into arbitrary cost-only behavior — fixed by validating weights BY NAME (UTILITY_WEIGHT_KEYS) in the top validation block. 2) The runtime portfolio forwarding at bt-ai-provider.ts was not behaviorally covered: ai-invariant-matrix runs both decision modes but its scenarios carry no utility-bearing optional objectives, so deleting the forwarding would have left the suite green — fixed by adding tests/unit/ai-objective-portfolio-wiring.test.ts (gated-forwarding + activeObjectiveId + lab/CLI reachability + per-persona weight completeness) and a real Floor 1 graph test where two weight profiles select DIFFERENT optional bundles.

Both reviewers independently verified LEGACY default-off parity (the utilityWeights branch continues on every path, leaving bestBundleCount unreachable in portfolio mode and untouched otherwise), determinism, required-goal safety, and canonical legacy sweep-config id stability. VALID+FIXED: (a) assertNonNegativeInteger on weights forbade fractional multipliers such as costPerSecond 0.5 (both reviewers) -> assertNonNegativeFinite; (b) weight validation was defined ~250 lines after the closure consuming it (opus) -> moved into the top validation block; (c) the Math.ceil whole-second overhead penalty was a step function charging a 1ms detour the same as a 1000ms one (gemini) -> linear penalty; (d) goal.utility dimensions were also integer-only (gemini; opus argued counts should stay integral) -> adjudicated toward gemini, one rule for every utility number, since exactness dies anyway once weights are fractional; (e) no test exercised costPerSecond > 0 or an equal-utility cost tie-break (both) -> added, with the linear case chosen so a ceil-based penalty would fail it. NOT VALID: negative selected utility scores under a high costPerSecond (opus) — the required-only mask scores 0 and correctly wins, so this is a tuning observation, not a defect.

independent_grade.notes: Round 1 (head 2eed19c) FAILED with one blocker: planFloor1ObjectiveRoute — which drives merchant/Spell-Broker purchase-intent admission off includedOptionalBundleIds — was never given utilityWeights, so under a contended budget it could admit a bundle the behavior tree's weighted route had already dropped. Fixed by routing both Floor 1 planner call sites through a single private strategicUtilityWeights() gate, plus a wiring guard pinning the call-site count and a behavioral run-planner test proving two personality profiles select different optional bundles while legacy stays byte-identical. Round 2 (head ffa5f11) found no high-confidence issues: dual call-site gating, required goals non-droppable, legacy default-off parity, partial/NaN weight rejection, linear cost penalty and persona divergence all covered. Weakest aspect is maintainability — several wiring guards assert on source-text slices (the repo's established pattern) and activeObjectiveId currently aliases routeHeadId.
